what: Every place the pipeline merged two descents at one hoop into a single call, judged one shot or two.
why: No measurement separates these. The gap between descents runs 0.02s to 0.87s, and how far the ball climbs in between runs 25px to 155px, with confirmed cases sitting mid-range in both. Wrists looked promising at 0.75 ball-widths for a catch against 1.18 for a bounce, but that was one example each.
the_finding: Clip 6 kills the simple version of the wrist rule. Orange CAUGHT the rebound and raised it behind the rim, then passed it back out instead of shooting. A rule keyed on 'someone caught it' calls that two shots and is wrong. Catching is necessary but not sufficient -- what follows the catch has to be a shot at the hoop, not a pass away from it.

so_what: TWO of the twelve calls are not shots at all -- a ball thrown in from the deck and someone dribbling on the concrete. Both are the deck again, which has now defeated five separate rules.
TWO are duplicates: the merge fired twice inside one event, so the pipeline emitted a pair of calls for a single shot.
Only 2 of 12 are genuine re-shoots, so the merge is usually right. It is wrong about 1 in 6, and both errors cost a real shot.
